messages.author: 0efd2d7533d4b99f
messages.subject: problem removing offset
parts:
Hi, I'm processing files recorded with SM3 and SM4 recorders, both affected by offset, that is different in the two channels.

In R/Seewave I'm doing this

        soundfile=readWave(filename)
        waveL=channel(soundfile,which="left")    # split the stereo wave in two mono wave objects
        waveR=channel(soundfile,which="right")
        rmoffset(waveL, FUN = mean, output="wave", plot=FALSE)
        rmoffset(waveR, FUN = mean, output="wave", plot=FALSE)

however my waveL and waveR still have their original offset and I see it any plot 

I also tried with this script: 

        CleanL=rmoffset(waveL, FUN = mean, output="wave", plot=FALSE)
        CleanR=rmoffset(waveR, FUN = mean, output="wave", plot=FALSE)

but when I then use 

  spectro(CleanL, osc=TRUE)

I get an error message saying that CleanL is not a wavs object

Are there others with the same problem ?   Or I'm wrong somewhere ?

Gianni

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] saving a spectrogram
parts:
Hi Gianni,

I am not sure to understand you request. If you mean that you wish to save the matrix of the spectrogram, you can do something like:

# get the spectro matrix
data(tico)
m <- spectro(tico, plot=FALSE)$amp
# save it as a csv file
write.table(m, file="tico-spectro.csv")

HTH

Jerome

messages.author: 65c82d09eac308cf
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] saving a spectrogram
parts:
Ok, use the function pdf() then, for instance :

data(tico)
d <- duration(tico)
time <- seq(0, d, by=d/4)

pdf("spectro.pdf")
for(i in 1:(length(time)-1))
    {
       spectro(tico, tlim=c(time[i], time[i+1]))
        }
dev.off()

But be carefull the final pdf might be bery heavy.

Best

Jerome
